correctness.rationale: Green's identity for the boundary-normalized solution gives \(\Lambda'(E_0)=1/(c|\psi_0(v_0)|^2)\), consistent with the standard Weyl-function derivative identity. Substituting this nonzero slope into Turek-Cheon's exact \(P_\alpha(E)=[1+\alpha^4F(E)^2]^{-1}\), with \(F=\Lambda/(2k)\), yields the local Lorentzian under the \(\alpha^{-2}\) scaling. The inverse-function expansion gives the two half-height roots; subtracting the two inverse-series branches cancels even powers and gives the \(O(\alpha^{-6})\) FWHM remainder. A change of variables gives the peak-area limit. The frozen interval verifier was read and its exact formula \(4ck_0L^{-1}\arctan(2/\alpha^2)\) has exactly the predicted expansion.
correctness.risk: The theorem is local to a simple visible nonthreshold resonance and excludes magnetic/multiple-resonance cases.

originality.rationale: The scientific conclusion is a direct local corollary of two established prior ingredients: Turek-Cheon publish the exact transmission probability in terms of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann function, while standard boundary-triplet/Weyl theory gives \(M(\lambda)-M(\mu)^*=(\lambda-\bar\mu)\gamma(\mu)^*\gamma(\lambda)\), whose real derivative is the squared norm of the boundary-normalized solution. In this scalar graph normalization that is exactly the reciprocal local spectral weight. Taylor expansion, inverse-function expansion and one Lorentzian integral then mechanically produce the linewidth and area formulas. Under the audit rule that direct corollaries are covered even without matching wording, the absence of a printed FWHM formula in the source does not establish originality.
